questions.question: How many countries share the international land border with India, as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India shares its land borders with seven countries.
 
• **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan** in the **northwest, China , Nepal,** and **Bhutan** in the **North **and **Myanmar** and **Bangladesh** in the** east.**
 
• Towards the south, India has two **neighbouring island countries - Sri Lanka and Maldives.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's geography is incredibly diverse. It includes:
 
 
• **The Himalayan Mountain Range: **In the north, it borders with the world's highest mountain range, which includes Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga, the world's highest and third highest peaks, respectively.
 
• **Northern Plains:** South of the Himalayas, there are fertile river plains, largely fed by rivers such as the Ganges, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra. These plains are densely populated and are the agricultural hub of the country.
 
• **Thar Desert: **To the west, in the state of Rajasthan and extending into Pakistan, is the arid Thar Desert.
 
• **Central Plateau:** Further south, there is the Deccan plateau, which is flanked by the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats, both of which are mountain ranges.
 
• **Coastal Plains:** On the western and eastern sides of the peninsula, there are narrow coastal plains that provide the country with a significant amount of coastline along the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, respectively.
 
• **Islands:** India also has several islands, the largest of which are Andaman and Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal and Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• These diverse geographical features contribute to India's rich biodiversity, with various ecosystems ranging from desert to rainforest, from high-altitude alpine conditions to fertile plains, and mangroves to coral reefs.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Rajasthan is also known as 'Sapera dance'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbelia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalbelia (Sapera Dance):** The Kalbelia dance, also known as the** 'Sapera'** or** 'Snake Charmer' **dance, is performed by the **Kalbelia tribe**. 
 
• The dance movements and costumes bear a resemblance to that of serpents, and the dance is characterized by** flexibility and graceful, sinuous movements.** 
 
• **The Kalbelia dance** is recognized by **UNESCO on its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Gair:**

 
• **Gair** is a folk dance popular in the **Rajasthan region**, specifically amongst the Bhil community.
 
• It's performed during Holi and other festive occasions.
 
• Men form a large circle and move clockwise and counter-clockwise, while dancing with large movements and twirling their colorful skirts.

**Chari:**

 
• **The Chari dance**, or pot dance, is performed predominantly by women who balance brass pots on their heads.
 
• The dance often involves spontaneous twirling and swirling, showcasing the dancers' skills in balancing the pots, often lit with a cotton seed lamp.
 
• This dance celebrates the joy of collecting water in the desert region.

**Ghoomar:**

 
• **Ghoomar** is one of the most famous folk dances in **Rajasthan**.
 
• It is performed by women in swirling robes, and is accompanied by men and women singing together.
 
• The term 'ghoomar' refers to the twirling movement that displays the spectacular colors of the flowing **'ghaghara',** the long skirt of the Rajasthani women.
 
• This dance form is also known for its grace and is often performed on special occasions.

questions.question: Which among the following planets does not have any satellite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jupiter:**

 
 
• **Jupiter** is the **largest planet in our solar system and it has the most number of confirmed moons as well. **
 
• The four largest, known as the **Galilean moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto), were discovered by Galileo Galilei in the early 17th century.**
 
 
 
• **Venus:**
 
 
• **Venus,** the second planet from **the sun** and our closest planetary neighbor, has **no natural moons**.
 
• While** Venus** is similar to **Earth in size and structure**, the lack of a moon is one of the many differences between the two planets.
 
 
 
• **Saturn:**
 
 
• **Saturn** is known for its extensive ring system, but it also has a large number of moons.
 
• Saturn has **145 confirmed moons**, the largest of which, **Titan,** is the second-largest moon in the solar system and is larger than the planet Mercury.
 
 
 
• **Uranus:**
 
 
• Uranus, the seventh planet from the Sun, has **27 known moons.**
 
• The names of all of the moons of Uranus are chosen from characters in the works of William Shakespeare and Alexander Pope.

questions.question: Materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them are called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulator**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulators: **
 
• Insulators are materials that do not allow the flow of electric current.
 
• **The electrons** in insulator materials are tightly bound to their atoms and do not move freely, thus preventing the flow of electric current.
 
• Examples of insulators include **rubber, glass, and most plastics.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conductors: **

 
 
• Conductors are materials that allow the flow of electric current.
 
• They have free electrons that can move easily between atoms.
 
• This movement of electrons is what we refer to as an electric current.
 
• Examples of good conductors include metals like copper, aluminum, and gold.
 
 
 
• **Capacitors:**
 
 
• Capacitors are not a type of material, but a type of component used in electronic circuits.
 
• A capacitor is a device that stores electrical energy in an electric field.
 
• It is made of two conductive plates separated by an insulator (also called a dielectric).
 
• When a voltage is applied across the plates, an electric field is created and energy is stored.
 
 
 
• **Inductors:**
 
 
• Like capacitors, inductors are also components used in electronic circuits, not a type of material.
 
• An inductor is a coil of wire that stores energy in a magnetic field when electric current flows through it.
 
• The property of an inductor to oppose a change in current is known as inductance.
 
• Inductors are often used in analog circuits and signal processing.

questions.question: Who among the following was revered as the 'Queen of Thumri'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Girija Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Girija Devi **is often revered as the** 'Queen of Thumri.' Girija Devi (1929 – 2017) **was an eminent Indian classical singer who performed classical and light classical music and popularized the genre of Thumri.
 
• She earned wide acclaim and numerous accolades for her soulful performances and rich contribution to Indian music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naina Devi:**

• **Siddheshwari Devi:**

• Known for her mastery over the emotive and romantic aspects of thumri, she made a significant impact on the Indian classical music scene.
 
 
 
• **Annapurna Devi:**

questions.question: Plants with green and tender stems are called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Herbs**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plants** with green and tender stems are called herbs.
 
• **Herbs** are usually short, non-woody plants.
 
• They might be **annuals, biennials, or perennials, but the common feature is their soft, green, and tender stem structure.**
 
• Examples of herbs include **grasses, ferns, and certain types of flowering plants.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shrubs**:

 
 
• Shrubs are medium-sized, semi-woody plants.
 
• They are usually multi-stemmed, smaller than trees, and have a bushy appearance.
 
• Shrubs can be both evergreen or deciduous. Examples of shrubs include holly, rose, and azalea.
 
 
 
• **Trees: **
 
 
• Trees are tall, woody plants.
 
• They typically have a single main stem or trunk that grows to a considerable height and bear lateral branches.
 
• Examples include oaks, maples, and pines. They play a crucial role in producing oxygen and sequestering carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Canopy: **
 
 
• Canopy refers to the overhead layer or habitat formed by mature tree crowns in a forest.
 
• It's not a type of plant, but rather a term that describes a particular layer within a forest ecosystem.
 
• The canopy provides shelter and habitat to various animals and plants.
 
 
 
• **Herbs: **
 
 
• Herbs are small, non-woody plants.
 
• They have green and tender stems.
 
• They usually die back to the ground at the end of each growing season.
 
• They can be annuals (life cycle completed in one growing season), biennials (life cycle completed in two growing seasons), or perennials (live for several to many growing seasons).
 
• Examples of herbs include basil, mint, and dill.

questions.question: Sex ratio in India is defined as the number of females per __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1000 males in the population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sex ratio** in India (and most other places) is typically defined as the number of females per **1000 males in the population**.
 
• It's a demographic measure used to indicate the proportion of** males to females in a population**.
 
• A higher sex ratio implies a larger number of females compared to males, and a lower sex ratio implies a larger number of males compared to females.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• By the **2011 census**, there were **46 'million-plus cities' in India**, with **Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata having populations over 10 million.**
 
• There are 53 urban agglomerations in India with a population of 1 million or more by the 2011 census.
 
• **According to the 2001 census**, there were **35 cities in India** that have more than **1 million population**.
 
• 31.165 % population can be categorized under Urban as per the **2011 Census.**
 
• By census 2011, Goa is the most urbanized state with 62.17% of the population living in urban areas.

questions.question: The Ravan Phadi cave in _________ is an example of the early Chalukya style architecture which is known for its distinct sculptural style.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ravan Phadi **cave is located in** Aihole**, in the **Bagalkot district of Karnataka, India**.
 
• This site is renowned for its historic temples and structures from the early **Chalukya dynasty,** which ruled the region from **the 6th to the 12th centuries.**
 
• **The Ravan Phadi cave** is a notable example of early Chalukya architecture, featuring intricate rock-cut sculptures and carvings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamil Nadu:**

 
 
• It is located in the **southernmost part of India, Tamil Nadu is known for its Dravidian-style Hindu temple**s.
 
• The state has a rich history of empires such as** the Chola, Pallava, Pandya, and Chera.** 
 
 
 
• **Kerala**:
 
 
• This southwestern Indian state is known for its scenic beauty including its backwaters, palm-lined beaches, and a network of canals.
 
• In addition, it has a rich cultural heritage with its own unique architecture and temple designs, often associated with the **ancient Chera Empire and later feudal kingdoms.**
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh: **
 
 
• It is Located in southeastern India, Andhra Pradesh has a history that dates back to the Vedic period.
 
• It has been ruled by several major Indian dynasties such as **the Maurya, Satavahana, and Chalukya**. 
 
 
 
• **Karnataka: **
 
 
• It is Located in the southwestern region of India, Karnataka was home to some of India's most powerful empires, such as the** Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara.**
 
• **The Ravan Phadi cave**, an example of early **Chalukya architecture,** is located in **Aihole in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka.**

questions.question: ​The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 seeks to increase the marriage age of women to _________ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill 2021, which seeks to enhance the legal minimum age of marriage of a girl from 18 to 21 across all religions was introduced in the Lok Sabha amid protests by the Opposition members on 21 Dec 2021.
 
• After the introduction of the Bill, it was sent to the Standing Committee of the Parliament for further discussion and scrutiny.
 
• Introducing the Bill in the House, the Women and Child Development Minister, Smriti Zubin Irani said that the Legislation will provide the right of equality to women across all religions and castes in marriages.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A special task force was constituted by the Union Ministry of Women and Child Development which was headed by Jaya Jaitly. 
 
• According to reports, the Government would soon introduce amendments to the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, personal laws such as the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and the Special Marriage Act.
 
• The committee has also recommended sex education be formalized and introduced into the school curriculum.

questions.question: Who won India's first badminton medal in Olympics games?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __Saina Nehwal__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Saina Nehwal is an Indian player who won the first Olympic medal in badminton in** London in 2012**.
 
• A former world no. 1, she has won over 24 international titles, including eleven titles in the Superseries.
 
• While she reached the 2nd world ranking in 2009, it was only in 2015 that she was able to cross the No. 1 world ranking, becoming the only female player from India and after Prakash Padukone, the second Indian player to achieve this feat.
 
• Three times at the Olympics, she has represented India, earning a bronze medal in her second appearance.
 
• She is the first Olympic medal-winning Indian badminton player, the first Indian to reach the final of the BWF World Championship, and the only Indian to win the BWF or Junior World Championships.
 
• She became the first Indian female to win a 4-star tournament in 2006 and the youngest Asian.
 
• She became the first Indian to win two Commonwealth Games singles gold medals (2010 and 2018).​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Srikanth Kidambi is an Indian badminton player who ranked in the BWF rankings in April 2018 as world number 1.
 
• Pullela Gopichand is a former player of Indian badminton who is the Indian Badminton team's, Chief National Coach. In 2001, he won the All England Open Badminton Championships, becoming the second Indian, after Prakash Padukone, to achieve this feat.
 
• Prakash Padukone is a former Indian badminton player; who was ranked World No. 1 in 1980. 
 
• **PV Sindhu **is the first Indian woman to win two Olympic medals - a silver in 2016 and a bronze in 2020.

 Sindhu is the only Indian to become the Badminton World Champion, achieving this feat in 2019.

 Her talent is reflected in her world ranking, having reached a career-high of No. 2 in 2017.

questions.question: The period of life, when the body undergoes changes leading to reproductive maturity is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**adolescence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Growing up is a natural process. The period of life, when the body undergoes changes, leading to reproductive maturity, is called adolescence.
 
• Adolescence is a phase of the life of a person when he is no more a child and not yet an adult. This is a critical time in life because the experiences, knowledge, and skills acquired in adolescence have important implications in adulthood.
 
• Adolescence begins around the age of 11 and lasts up to 18 or 19 years of age. The period of adolescence varies from person to person.
 
• The human body undergoes several changes during adolescence. These changes mark the onset of puberty. Puberty ends when an adolescent reaches reproductive maturity. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infancy:** From birth up to the 2nd year of life, the stage is known as infancy. Babies grow very rapidly in size during their first two years. The acquisition of motor skills like holding things, crawling, walking proceeds from simple to complex.
 
• **Childhood**: It extends from 2 to 12 years and is generally divided into early and late childhood.
 
• **Adulthood:** It is the stage where growth is complete and the person assumes various responsibilities. Starting around 18 years it extends till middle age which is around 45 years.

questions.question: Cultivation of rice needs high rainfall with __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High temperature and high humidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rice is the most important food crop of India covering about one-fourth of the total cropped area and providing food to about half of the Indian population.

 
 
• The rice is cultivated in the largest areas in India.
 
• Rice cultivation in India extends from 8 to35ºN latitudes and from sea level to as high as 3000 meters.
 
• The Rice crop needs a hot and humid climate__.
 
• It is best suited to regions that have high humidity, prolonged sunshine, and an assured supply of water.
 
• The average temperature required throughout the life period of the crop ranges from 21 to 37º C.
 
• 
 
The average annual rainfall required by rice is 150 cm. ​

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Tea bush is a tropical and sub-tropical plant **and thrives well in a hot and humid climate.

 
 
• The ideal temperature for its growth is 20°-30°C and temperatures above 35°C and below 10°C are harmful to the bush.
 
• The average annual rainfall required by rice is 150 cm-300 cm.
 
• Tea is grown in 16 states in India eg -Darrang, Goalpara, Kamrup, Lakhimpur, Dibrugarh, Nowgong, Sibsagar, Cachar, Karbi Anlong, etc.
 
 
 
• **Coffee** is grown in three regions of India in Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
 
• The coffee plant requires a hot and humid climate with temperatures varying between 15°C and 28 °C and rainfall from 150 to 250 cm.
 
• It does not tolerate frost, snowfall, high temperatures above 30°C, and strong sunshine.

questions.question: Who among the following Governor Generals of Bengal outlawed the practice of Sati?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __William Bentinck__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck (1828-1835)

 
 
• ​​During his tenure as Governor- General following were the various events that took place:
 
• Abolition of Sati and other cruel rites (1829).
 
• Suppression of thugs (1830).
 
• Charter Act of 1833.
 
• Resolution of 1835, and educational reforms and introduction of English as the official language.
 
• Annexation of Mysore (1831), Coorg (1834), and Central Cachar (1834).
 
• Treaty of 'perpetual friendship with Ranjeet Singh.
 
• Abolished the provincial court of appeal and circuit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Canning

 
 
• He was an English statesman and Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• He was the Governor-General of India from 1856 - 1858 and viceroy from 1858 - 1862.
 
• He was the first Viceroy of India after the transfer of power from the East India Company to the Crown of Queen Victoria in 1858.
 
• After the rebellion, he presided over a smooth transfer and reorganization of government from the East India Company to the crown.
 
• He is credited with establishing the first three modern Universities in India, the University of Calcutta, the University of Madras, and the University of Bombay based on Wood's despatch.
 
• Canning also passed the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, of 1856 which was drafted by his predecessor Lord Dalhousie before the rebellion.​​​
 
 
 
• Lord Dalhousie:
 
 
• James Andrew Brown-Ramsay also known as Lord Dalhousie.
 
• He served as governor-general of India from 1848-1856.
 
• James Outram was made the British Resident of Awadh in place of Sleeman.
 
• He said that the administration of Awadh is very corrupt and the condition of the people is very contemplative.
 
• Outram's report was the basis for the annexation of Awadh.
 
• Lord Dalhousie annexed the Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah on February 13, 1856, accusing him of misrule.
 
• Apart from Awadh, under the principle of Doctrine of Lapse, the merged territories- Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854), and Karauli (1855).
 
• The first attempt towards railway construction in India was made by Lord Dalhousie in 1853 AD.
 
• It was laid between Bombay to Thane at the time of Dalhousie.
 
• The last expansion of British Indian territory took place during Dalhousie.
 
• During his tenure, for the first time, a separate public Works Department was created.
 
 
 
• Lord Warren Hastings
 
 
• In 1781, Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, established a madrasa in Calcutta for the study and teaching of Muslim law.
 
• Calcutta Madrasa, The (later Calcutta Aliya Madrasa) was the earliest of the state-managed educational institutions under British rule in India.
 
• Founded by Governor-General Warren Hastings in October 1780 with its entire expense borne by him for a year and a half, of course fully reimbursed later, the Bengal Government took it over in April 1782.
 
• Originally situated at Baithakkhana near Sealdah in Calcutta.
 
• It was shifted to its present site at Wellesley Square in 1827.

questions.question: Article 43B of the Indian constitution provide for __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promotion of cooperative societies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 43B

 
 
• Article 43B deals with the promotion of cooperative societies.
 
• The State shall endeavour to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies. [Article 43B Inserted by the 97th Constitution Amendment Act, 2011
 
 
 
• ​Directive principle of state policy
 
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy are stated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It contains Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSPs are non-binding in nature which means they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• These principles emphasize that the State shall try to promote the welfare of the people by providing them with basic facilities like shelter, food, and clothing.
 
• It denotes the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws.
 
• Article 51 is the last Directive Principle of State Policy in the constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental duty

 
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee is related to the Fundamental Duties in India.
 
• On the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, 11 Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 51A deals with the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• There are 11 fundamental duties, they are:
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect the national flag & National Anthem.
 
• Follow the ideals of the freedom struggle.
 
• Protect the sovereignty & integrity of India.
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon.
 
• Spirit of a common brotherhood.
 
• Preserve composite culture.
 
• Preserve the natural environment.
 
• Develop a scientific temper.
 
• Safeguard public property.
 
• Strive for excellence.
 
• Duty for all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.
 
 

 
• Fundamental Rights

 
 
• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12-35). Part III of the Constitution is described as the Magna Carta of India.
 
• ‘Magna Carta’, the Charter of Rights issued by King John of England in 1215 was the first written document relating to the Fundamental Rights of citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are justiciable because when violated the aggrieved individual can move the courts for their enforcement.
 
• The Supreme Court or High Courts have the power to issue directions or orders or writs for the enforcement of any of the Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of Vinegar?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __Acetic Acid.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical name of vinegar is acetic acid__.
 
• Acetic acid is also called ethanoic acid.
 
• Chemical formula- CH3COOH
 
• Vinegar is made from the fermentation of ethanol (grain alcohol) by bacteria from the family Acetobacteraceae.
 
• It consists of acetic acid, water, and trace amounts of other chemicals, which may include flavorings.
 
• Spirit vinegar is a strong variety of vinegar (5% to 21% acetic acid) made from sugar cane and doubly fermented.
 
• The first fermentation changes sugar into alcohol, while the second fermentation changes alcohol into acetic acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 Citric acid

 
• Citric acid is present in citrus fruits like lemon, orange, pomelo, etc.
 
• The common name of citric acid is sour salt.
 
• It has the chemical formula C6H8O7.

Lactic acid

 
• Lactic acid is generally present in milk, yogurt, pickled foods, etc.
 
• It is also present in the human body's red blood cells and muscle cells.
 
• The chemical formula for lactic acid is C3H6O3.

Formic Acid:

 
• The acid to which the hydrogen atom is attached to the carboxylic (COOH) group is known as formic acid.
 
• The formula of formic acid is HCOOH.
 
• It has an IUPAC name as methanoic acid.
 
• It is present in the stings of ants and bees.
 
• It is poisonous in nature.
 
• It is the first acid in the list of carboxylic acids.
 
• it is a weak acid and is used as an antibacterial agent.

• she won four gold medals in the Rio Olympics, had entered the Tokyo Games with high expectations but has been praised by many fellow athletes for prioritising her mental health and drawing attention to the pressure put on young Olympians.
 
• After further consultation with medical staff, Simone Biles has decided to withdraw from the event finals for the vault and the uneven bars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Table-tennis:

__
 
• Table tennis was invented in England in the early days of the 20th century and was originally called Ping-Pong, a trend name.
 
• It is a ball game similar to lawn tennis and played on a flat table divided into two equal courts by a net fixed across its width in the middle.
 
• The object is to hit the ball so that it goes over the net and bounces on the opponent’s half of the table so that the opponent cannot reach it or return it correctly.
 
• The lightweight hollow ball is propelled back and forth across the net by small rackets (bats, or paddles) held by the players.
 
• The game is famous all over the world.
 
• In most countries, it is highly organized as a competitive sport, especially in Europe and Asia, particularly China and Japan.

​Badminton

 
• ​__Lawn, court, or badminton game played with a shuttlecock and lightweight rackets.
 
• The shuttlecock, commonly referred to as a "bird" or "birdie," was historically a little cork hemisphere with 16 goose feathers sewn on it that weighed about 0.17 ounces (5 grams).
 
• Modern play may still employ these shuttles, although the Badminton World Federation also permits the use of synthetic shuttles.
 
• The game is called after Badminton, which was initially played around 1873 at the duke of Beaufort's country home in Gloucestershire, England.
 
• Poona, a game played by British army officers stationed in India in the 1860s, is directly related to badminton.
 
• In 1899, the first unofficial all-England men's badminton championships and the inaugural badminton competition for women were arranged the next year.
 
• Badminton made its Olympic debut in 1972 as a demonstration sport and in 1988 as an exhibition sport. It was made a full-medal Olympic sport for the 1992 Games, including competition in the men's and women's singles (one against one) and doubles events (two against two). The mixed pairs event debuted in the 1996 Olympics.
 
• As per the guidelines laid down by the Badminton World Federation (BWF), the length of a standard badminton court remains the same - 13.40m (44 feet) - for both types of competitions.
